payload.label: Sort mail into my built-in task lists
payload.job: Say which built-in to-do list (calendar, email or other) each email would become a task in when I turn my mail into tasks
payload.description: Give messages (at most 50, each { subject?, from?, labels?, list_unsubscribe?, has_invite? }). Each is tested against the email_split rows of calendar-tasks.json in order (an invite or invitation subject goes to calendar; a list-unsubscribe header, a promotions, updates, social, forums or spam label, or unsubscribe in the subject goes to other; anything else to email), and the first row that matches names its list. Answers messages ({ index, subject, smart_list }) and counts per list. It reads only the messages it is given: it reads no mailbox, makes and saves no task, and sends nothing. The Calendar task screen (calendar-tasks.mjs, kept in this folder but not run here) does the rest of the old job: it keeps named task lists with counts, groups and sorts them, schedules a task onto a day or time, and saves each email as a task with its title, priority, duration, deadline and repeat rule. That needs the records store and the timed-action parts, which this run does not have.

payload.label: See who can take my work: which people, AIs and other records are live, what each can do and how many tasks each holds
payload.job: Show me who I can hand a task to: which are live now, what each can do and how many tasks each is doing
payload.description: Reads every record handed in that is not a task (a person, an AI, a raccoon, anything with a record) and answers each with its id, its whole stored value (every cell as kept: a caller names it from those cells by its own formula; no name is made here), whether it is live (seen within the minutes its record names as live.minutes, else task-moves.json live_minutes_default), when it was last seen, and how many tasks it holds as taker. Live ones come first, then by the order cell. `can` keeps only those that can do every word given (one that can do any can do all); `live_only` keeps only the live ones. Nothing is written. The caller hands in every record it reads as input.records; this tool reads no store and names no store method. Each write it makes comes back as keep, for the caller to keep in the person's own store.

payload.label: Give a task to anyone: a person, an AI, another record, or whoever takes it first
payload.job: Make a new task, waiting for the ones named to take it, or for anyone when none is named
payload.description: Writes one task, id record:calendar-task:<key>, with status To do, its title (title, else the first line of description), its description, its outcome (what done looks like), its priority (urgent, high, medium or low; medium when left out), sent_by (as: the record id of whoever gives it), sent_at, and assignees: the record ids of anyone who may take it. An empty or missing list means anyone may take it, and every assignee must be among the records handed in. source {kind, ref} keeps where it came from; obligations declare parts each checked on its own; acceptance saves the checks a finish must pass. key (or the run's request key) names the task: the write is conditioned on the task being absent, so the same key gives the task once; sending it again answers written with no write, and a different task under the same key answers already-there. The caller hands in every record it reads as input.records; this tool reads no store and names no store method. Each write it makes comes back as keep, for the caller to keep in the person's own store.

payload.label: Take the next task waiting for me, or one task by its id
payload.job: Take the next task that is waiting for me or for anyone, so no one else does it too
payload.description: Without id, reads the tasks a take may move (waiting ones that name `as` or no one, and taken ones held longer than the stale-take time), sorts them by take_order (priority, then oldest first), and takes the first: one write of the whole task as taken by as at this time, conditioned on the value it read. When someone else took that task first the write is refused and changes nothing, and the next one is tried, at most take_tries. only_mine keeps only tasks that name as. With id, takes that task, or answers taken null with reason changed (and the task as it now is) when someone else won it. taken is null when there was nothing to take. The same request key gives back the same claim. The caller hands in every record it reads as input.records; this tool reads no store and names no store method. Each write it makes comes back as keep, for the caller to keep in the person's own store.

payload.label: Finish, fail, give back, hand on, withdraw, flag or remove a task
payload.job: Record what happened to a task: finish it with its result, say it failed, give it back, hand it on to someone else, say what blocks it, take back one I gave, or remove it
payload.description: Reads the task id and makes the move action names, by the rules in task-moves.json: finish (the taker; needs result, may add summary and check) and fail (the taker; needs result: why) end it as Done or Broken; release gives it back to To do (the taker, or anyone once it is held longer than the stale-take time; because says why); hand-on replaces the assignees (required) and gives the task back to To do with no taker (the taker, or the giver while it waits); stuck says what blocks it (anyone, so a watcher can flag it; needs words) and unstuck clears that; withdraw takes back a task still waiting (its giver; because); wait keeps recoverable work blocked on this same task with continuation {owner, action, after, reason}; resume returns it to waiting when due (its taker, giver or continuation owner); plan saves the acceptance a finish checks (the taker); edit changes a waiting task's words, assignees or acceptance (its giver); remove deletes the record (its giver, or anyone once it is finished). The move is one write of the whole task conditioned on the value just read: when the task changed meanwhile nothing is written and the answer is moved false with reason changed and the task as it now is. A move the rules do not allow is refused, saying why. A finish also needs check: the exact saved outcome, checked_at during this take, consumer evidence ({ref, observation}), and one matching check per saved obligation. This records accountable observation and does not itself prove its truth. The caller hands in every record it reads as input.records; this tool reads no store and names no store method. Each write it makes comes back as keep, for the caller to keep in the person's own store.
